review_scope: Primary read the full first-pass report and independently read env.json, task.json, controls.json, generator, browser JavaScript, mechanic CSS, grader, task verifier, solver, and shared verifier_helpers.py.
decision: Keep all baseline labels and the L1-L2 exploration No exception in both interaction modes. World-space contact, persistent flight-vector control and forward-only motion support 3D, temporal and consequential trajectory choice. Some baseline routes hide the first seal completely outside the canvas; steering is required to discover it.

rationale_clarifications.exploration_interface: The L1-L2 No exception does not rely on the JavaScript's expanded draw-culling window being visible. L1 seals are in the initial canvas. At the L2 extreme, a first-seal center can lie just beyond the top/bottom edge (|y|<=34, z>=60 implies center y in [-13.34,553.34]), but its glow radius is at least 2.6*16*38/76=20.8 pixels. This provides an initial visible directional cue even at the extreme; the later waypoints are farther away with contracted lateral/vertical offsets. Such direct steering toward an already visible cue does not require a separate information-discovery action. L3-L5 allow seals with no visible part until the camera is steered.

additional_source_evidence.claim: L1-L2 spans and first target depth bounds; later target offsets contract and depths increase.
Perspective projection, depth-scaled glow radius, and the distinction between off-canvas drawing and visible canvas content.

uncertainties: Source-supported annotation only; no human or screenshot-only agent run was performed, and no success-rate or difficulty calibration is claimed.
